question: Which of these models is generative, i.e. models how the features are distributed within each class?

answers.feedback: Correct! LDA models P(X | Y) and P(Y), and then uses Bayes' theorem to obtain P(Y | X).
Not quite. Logistic regression models P(Y | X) directly, so it is discriminative.
Not quite. Linear regression is not a classification model and does not model the distribution of the predictors.

question: Why does LDA produce a linear decision boundary?

answers.answer: All classes share one covariance matrix, so the quadratic term is the same for all classes and cancels
answers.feedback: Correct! In QDA, every class has its own covariance matrix, so the quadratic term remains.

answers.answer: The features are assumed to be uncorrelated
answers.feedback: Not quite. LDA allows correlated features, as long as the correlation is the same in all classes.

answers.answer: The prior probabilities are assumed to be equal
answers.feedback: Not quite. The priors shift the boundary, but they have no influence on its shape.

question: You have 10 features and 3 classes. How many covariance parameters does QDA have to estimate?

answers.feedback: Correct! Each class has its own covariance matrix with 10 × 11 / 2 = 55 parameters, so 3 × 55 = 165. LDA only needs 55.
Not quite. This is the number for one covariance matrix, which is all LDA needs. How many matrices does QDA need?
Not quite. A covariance matrix for p features has p(p+1)/2 parameters, and QDA estimates one matrix per class.

question: You have only 40 observations, 15 features, and no reason to expect different covariances between the classes. Which model would you try first?

answers.feedback: Correct! With few observations, QDA has too many parameters to estimate. LDA has more bias, but much less variance.
Not quite. QDA needs a separate covariance matrix per class, which is hard to estimate from so few observations.

question: What is the effect of the term log(π_k) in the discriminant function?

answers.answer: It favors classes that are more common in the training data
answers.feedback: Correct! π_k is the prior probability of class k. If a class is common, an observation needs less evidence to be assigned to it.

answers.answer: It accounts for the correlation between the features
answers.feedback: Not quite. This is the role of the covariance matrix.

answers.answer: It makes the decision boundary quadratic
answers.feedback: Not quite. The term does not depend on X, so it only shifts the boundary.
